verdict.rationale: Grok Build is documented as a coding agent. In plan mode it explores the codebase, drafts a plan for approval, and then edits, and session snapshots can restore all files to an earlier state. Community users report it performed well on real projects. However, no evidence explicitly shows a plain-language feature or bug request being implemented across multiple files, so only the core agentic edit loop is evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit documentation or hands-on examples of multi-file feature implementation or bug fixing from a natural-language request, and independent corroboration of bug-fix workflows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have the agent implement or fix it across multiple files

citations.quote: Grok Build is a powerful and extensible coding agent.
In plan mode the agent explores the codebase and drafts a plan for your approval before it edits anything.
Selecting one restores all files to their state at that point and truncates the conversation to match.
Grok Build has had impressive performance in a couple of my projects.
